issues: P2 — reload_state silently reuses cached state when a previously existing state.json disappears. __init__ can load accepted phases and run history, but reload_state only replaces self.state when the file exists. If the checkpoint is accidentally removed before reload, validation checks the old in-memory copy and succeeds; a subsequent refresh/save recreates that copy as canonical state. This conceals checkpoint loss and can resurrect outdated acceptance or discard newer history if the instance's snapshot is older. Repair: distinguish a genuinely new controller from one that has observed or committed persisted state. Under the writer lock, veto a missing checkpoint after persistence has been observed; require explicit evidence-preserving recovery instead of silently saving cached state. Preserve normal first-run initialization.
next_actions: Add a regression covering checkpoint disappearance after construction and before reload; require a continuation veto and no replacement checkpoint or derived plan.
Also cover disappearance after a successful save on an initially new controller, while retaining a successful clean first-run case.
Rerun the relevant controller checks and submit the bounded repair for fresh review.
residuals: Lock acquisition, atomic-write durability, process cleanup, repair execution and approval installation are supplied as interfaces rather than implementations in this packet; this review does not independently establish them.

refresh commits canonical state before publishing derived views. Ordinary interruption can therefore leave older derived files temporarily present.
